title: Nintendo Sold a 1999 Fire Emblem Only at Convenience Store Kiosks
hook:
In September 1999, three years after the N64 launched, Nintendo put out a new Super Famicom Fire Emblem you could only get by having it written onto a blank cartridge at a Lawson convenience store. Would you have lined up for it?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Nintendo released a brand new Super Famicom game in 1999, three years after the Nintendo 64 came out? That game was Fire Emblem Thracia seven seventy six, the fifth game in the series. And at first, you could not buy it on a normal cartridge. It launched on September 1, 1999, only through a service called Nintendo Power. You bought a blank rewritable cartridge, carried it into a Lawson convenience store, and had the game written onto it at a kiosk. Nintendo also sold a deluxe pack with the game already loaded. A regular cartridge did not arrive until January 2000, by which point the Dreamcast was already on shelves. The game itself was brutal. It added a fatigue system, so a unit that fought too much had to sit out the next chapter. Enemies could capture your units and carry them away. Some maps did not ask you to win at all, only to escape. Nintendo Life said its difficulty was in another league compared with the rest of the series. It was also the last Fire Emblem built for the Super Famicom. It stayed a Japan only release for years, and fans finished a full English translation in 2019. Would you have lined up at a convenience store for it? Follow for more gaming history.
